title: Clipped direction gives head displacement
statement: For every natural number $n$, input-head position $p\in\{0,\ldots,n+1\}$, and direction $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$, let the head move by $d$ with clamping at the two boundary positions, and let the clipped direction be $0$ for an attempted move outward at a boundary and $d$ otherwise. The resulting head position, shifted down by one, is $p-1$ plus the clipped direction.
hypotheses_covered: direction d in the sign type
replaced:
For every input head position $p \in \{0, 1, \dots, n+1\}$ and every direction $d$,
the position reached by the native clamped input move of $p$ in direction $d$, shifted
down by one, equals $p - 1$ plus the clipped direction viewed as an integer.
